from.fees: None — no climbing fee (National Forest, not Mount Rainier NP)
from.rules: Group size capped at 12 (people + stock combined) inside Glacier Peak Wilderness; larger groups must split with 1-mile separation. Campfires prohibited above 3,500 ft in wilderness.
from.permit: None required — free self-issue wilderness permits available at trailheads/ranger stations for day/overnight travel where the peak is inside designated wilderness.
from.land_manager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Darrington Ranger District)
from.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Mountain Loop Highway trailheads — $5/day or $30/year.

HELD, no value proposed: Mountain Project gives mixed belays (a tree with slings at the top of P1, with a chain belay 15 ft away; chains at the top of P4, about 50 ft below and right of the big tree). No single anchor type fits the column.

wa_the_big_tree.notes: FA 'Manuel Gonzalez, Don Williamson (1970)' and commitment II both match Mountain Project, but an FA never locks from one source and a commitment grade from MP alone is held, so no ledger entries. CATALOG NOTE (pair to report, not a duplicate to merge): wa_three_o_clock_rock_big_tree_2 stores 5.8- trad, 4 pitches, 152 m, which are the exact figures Mountain Project prints on BOTH its The Big Tree and Big Tree 2 pages (same FA party and year on both). The two are different lines that share the first pitch (Big Tree II goes right from the P1 tree and uses two bolts of Shake, Rattle and Roll), so the identical length and pitch count on Big Tree 2 look copied from the Big Tree page rather than measured for that line. wa_three_o_clock_rock_big_tree_2000 (5.10a, 2 pitches) is a third related line. MP also names an older original first pitch from the Cornucopia Flake, and the 2015 CascadeClimbers report describes a newer two-pitch extension above the route (Shake, Rattle and Roll) that has no catalog row. MP says none of these lines are set up for a single-rope descent.
